Arrange the following four sentences from a fictional account in a coherent order.
(A) The account concludes with a note that this sequence establishes the order of Jaya's actions without making an outside claim about the plant itself.
(B) In the fictional account, Jaya first noticed that a plant's label had become unreadable.
(C) Having found the recorded name, she wrote it on a new label.
(D) After noticing this, she checked the plant's identity in the garden's own planting record and found its recorded name.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: B precedes D because “this” in D refers to the unreadable label noticed in B. D precedes C because Jaya finds the recorded name while checking the planting record, and C says she writes it after finding that name. A comes last because it states that the account concludes with this note.

topic: Match the Following: focus on this supplied section: taking care to do things carefully and correctly. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
Match each case in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes the stated action or preference. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) Before sending a spreadsheet, Asha checks each figure and corrects any errors so that the work is done carefully and correctly.
(B) On a forest walk, Imran watches for signs of danger or trouble.
(C) In a brief notice, Tara uses few words and includes only necessary and important information.
(D) At a community gathering, Kabir enjoys being with other people.

List-II
(I) "gregarious"
(II) "conscientious"
(III) "vigilant"
(IV) "concise"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Asha takes care to do her work carefully and correctly, so her action is conscientious. Imran watches for danger or trouble, Tara gives only necessary information using few words, and Kabir likes being with other people; these correspond to vigilant, concise and gregarious, respectively.

body: At a review meeting, Mira is asked for her view of a proposal. She openly and honestly says that she opposes it. A second reviewer privately also opposes it but deliberately gives a vague reply so the group will not learn her actual view. Which phrase describes the second reviewer’s response as an antonym of “candid”?
options: ["Stating one's genuine view openly and honestly","Checking details carefully before replying","Replying only at irregular intervals","Hiding one's genuine view behind a vague reply"]
explanation: “Candid” means saying what one thinks openly and honestly, without hiding one's thoughts. The second reviewer deliberately hides her actual view behind a vague reply, so D describes the opposite of that openness and honesty. Whether a view is favourable or critical does not determine whether it is candid.

Read the sentence and choose the phrase closest in meaning to “inevitable” as used here.
The village’s only road crossed a bridge that was closed for the day, and no alternative route was available. The delivery could not reach the village that day; a delay was inevitable.

body:
Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent account.
(A) Each member then practised the assigned part individually.
(B) Finally, they performed the scene together using the parts they had practised.
(C) After reading it, they assigned its speaking parts.
(D) At a fictional rehearsal, the group first read a short scene together.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Sentence (D) introduces the scene and says the group first read it. The cue “After reading it” places sentence (C) next, and “then” places individual practice in sentence (A) after the parts are assigned. “Finally” marks sentence (B) as the concluding event.

body:
Match each case in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) An assistant shows care and effort in completing assigned duties.
(B) An auditor pays careful attention to every detail while checking a file.
(C) A staff member is able to perform many different kinds of tasks.
(D) A colleague is aggressive or unfriendly and ready to argue.

List-II
(I) "meticulous"
(II) "diligent"
(III) "hostile"
(IV) "versatile"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The assistant is "diligent" because the case describes care and effort in carrying out duties. The auditor is "meticulous" because the case emphasises attention to every detail; the other two cases correspond to "versatile" and "hostile", respectively.

explanation: "Sparse" means present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area. In C, the broad plateau and long stretches of open ground between the houses show that they are few and widely spread. The other options describe crowded or frequent presence, which does not fit this sense.

body:
Match each case in List-I with the combination of effort and duration stated in List-II. For this question, "arduous" means involving a lot of effort and energy, especially over a period of time. Treat six months as a long period and five minutes as brief.

List-I
(A) A six-month project demands a great deal of effort and energy throughout.
(B) A repair demands a great deal of effort and energy for five minutes.
(C) Routine checks continue over six months but require little effort and energy.
(D) A brief, simple task requires little effort and energy.

List-II
(I) A great deal of effort and energy over a long period
(II) A great deal of effort and energy, but only briefly
(III) Little effort and energy over a long period
(IV) Little effort and energy, and only briefly

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A. (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
B. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
C. (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)
D. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
explanation: Case (A) combines a great deal of effort and energy with a long period, so it matches (I); cases (B), (C) and (D) match (II), (III) and (IV), respectively. This matches the stem’s definition of "arduous", which links the word to a lot of effort and energy, especially over a period of time.

topic: Vocabulary: test "plausible" in the supplied dictionary sense; use a short context where it disambiguates the answer.
body: An employee explains an absence by saying that a road closure forced a long detour. The supervisor considers this explanation "plausible", although she has not independently checked it. Which phrase is the antonym of "plausible" as used here?
options: ["Reasonable, but unlikely to be true","Unreasonable, but not independently verified","Reasonable and likely to be true","Unreasonable and unlikely to be true"]
explanation: Here, "plausible" means reasonable and likely to be true. Its antonym must oppose both qualities, so "unreasonable and unlikely to be true" is correct. Option A reverses only likelihood, while option B introduces verification status, which is not part of the stated meaning.

(B) After counting the notebooks, he recorded the count on the receipt and placed them in the cupboard.
(C) Ravi received a sealed parcel addressed to his class.
(D) Once he had confirmed that the address matched the receipt, Ravi opened the parcel and counted the notebooks inside.

body:
Match each description in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once. Use only the feature stated in each description.

List-I
(A) A person can design posters, repair bicycles, translate short texts, teach music and organise events.
(B) An object is known to be real and what it is claimed to be, rather than a copy.
(C) An explanation is logical, well organised and easy to understand.
(D) Plants are present in small numbers and spread over a large area.

List-II
(I) Coherent
(II) Versatile
(III) Sparse
(IV) Authentic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The person in (A) can do many different things, so the best match is versatile. The object in (B) is authentic, the explanation in (C) is coherent, and the plants in (D) are sparse.

explanation: “Reluctant” means hesitating before doing something because one does not want to do it. In D, Mira hesitates to address the audience because she does not want to speak before a large group; in the other sentences, the stated reasons are uncertainty, inability, or eagerness.

body: During a confidential schedule change, Nila checked her notices for accuracy and kept them brief. She was discreet when she withheld the unpublished detail, but later carelessly posted it in a public group. Which phrase expresses the antonym of “discreet” as used here?
options: ["Careless in what one says or does, allowing a secret to be revealed","Careful in carrying out a task correctly","Brief, giving only necessary information in few words","Able to recover quickly after an upsetting event"]
explanation: Here, “discreet” means being careful in what one says or does in order to keep something secret. Carelessly revealing that information expresses the opposite. The other options describe careful task performance, brevity, and recovery after an unpleasant event.

explanation: P has not paid the full amount called, so the ₹150 shortfall is calls in arrears; maintaining a separate Calls-in-Arrears Account is not mandatory. Q’s ₹150 excess is paid for an amount not yet called, so it is calls in advance, for which a separate account is maintained.

Any amount paid by a shareholder in the excess of the amount due from him on allotment/call (calls) is known as ‘Calls in Advance’ for which a separate account is maintained. A company has the power to charge interest on calls in arrears and is under an obligation to pay interest on calls-in-advance if it accepts them in accordance with the provisions of Articles of Association. Over Subscription: It is possible for the shares of some companies to be over subscribed which means that applications for more shares are received than the number offered for subscription. If the amount of minimum subscription is not received to the extent of 90%, the issue dissolves. In case the applications received are less than the number of shares offered to the public, the issue is termed as ‘under subscribed’. Issue of Shares at Premium: Irrespective of the fact that shares have been issued for consideration other than cash, they can be issued either at par or at premium. The issue of shares at par implies that the shares have been issued for an amount exactly equal to their face or nominal value. In case shares are issued at a premium, i.e. at an amount more than the nominal or par value of shares, the amount of premium is credited to a separate account called ‘Securities Premium Reserve Account’, the use of which is strictly regulated by law. Issue of Shares at Discount: Shares can as well be issued at a discount, i.e. for an amount less than the nominal or par value of shares provided the company fully complies with the provisions laid down by law with regard to the same. Apart from such compliance, shares of a company cannot ordinarily be issued at a discount. According to the Companies Act, 2013, only sweat equity shares can be issued at a discount. When shares are issued at a discount, the amount of discount is debited to ‘Discount on Issue of Share Account’, which is in the nature of capital loss for the company. Forfeiture of Shares: Sometimes, shareholders fail to pay one or more instalments on shares allotted to them. In such a case, the company has the authority to forfeit shares of the defaulters. This is called ‘Forfeiture of Shares’. Forfeiture means the cancellation of allotment due to breach of contract and to treat the amount already received on such shares as forfeited to the company. The precise accounting treatment of share forfeiture depends upon the conditions on which the shares have been issued — at par, premium or discount. Generally speaking, accounting treatment on forfeiture is to reverse the entries passed till the stage of forfeiture, the amount already received on the shares being credited to Forfeiture Shares Account. body: A company forfeited 400 shares of ₹10 each after ₹6 per share had been received on each share. It reissues 150 of these shares as fully paid for ₹8 per share. Assume the amount received is attributable equally to each forfeited share; no other shares are reissued and no other amounts are involved. What amount should be transferred to Capital Reserve in respect of this reissue?
explanation: The amount forfeited relating to the 150 reissued shares is 150 × ₹6 = ₹900. The reissue discount is 150 × (₹10 − ₹8) = ₹300, which is debited to the Forfeited Share Account. The balance relating to the reissued shares, ₹900 − ₹300 = ₹600, is transferred to Capital Reserve.

body:
On admission of a new partner, the old and new profit shares of the four existing partners are given below. Each fraction is a share of the firm’s total profit; the incoming partner receives the residual share.
List-I
(A) P: old share 1/2; new share 2/5
(B) Q: old share 1/4; new share 1/5
(C) R: old share 1/6; new share 2/15
(D) S: old share 1/12; new share 1/15
List-II
(I) 1/20
(II) 1/60
(III) 1/10
(IV) 1/30
Match List-I with List-II to identify each existing partner’s sacrifice of profit share. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A partner’s sacrifice is the old share of profit minus the new share. Thus P sacrifices 1/2 − 2/5 = 1/10, Q sacrifices 1/4 − 1/5 = 1/20, R sacrifices 1/6 − 2/15 = 1/30, and S sacrifices 1/12 − 1/15 = 1/60, which gives option D.

The ratio is normally clearly given as agreed among the partners which could be the old ratio, equal sacrifice, or a specified ratio. The difficulty arises where the ratio in which the new partner acquires his share from the old partners is not specified. Instead, the new profit sharing ratio is given. body:
A company is preparing a common-size balance sheet and a common-size statement of profit and loss. Consider the following statements about the percentage bases to use:
(A) Inventory in the balance sheet is expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(B) Each liability item in the balance sheet is expressed as a percentage of total liabilities.
(C) An expenditure item in the statement of profit and loss is expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(D) An expenditure item in the statement of profit and loss is expressed as a percentage of total liabilities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(A), (B) and (C) only","(A) and (B) only"]
explanation: In a common-size balance sheet, each asset is expressed as a percentage of total assets, while each liability is expressed as a percentage of total liabilities. In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations; therefore, only (A) and (B) are correct.

Here, each item in the statement is stated as a percentage of the aggregate, or revenue from operations of which that item is a part. For example, a common size balance sheet shows the percentage of each asset to the total assets, and that of each liability to the total liabilities. Similarly, in the common size statement of profit and loss, the items of expenditure are shown as a percentage of the revenue from operations. If such a statement is prepared for successive periods, it shows the changes of the respective percentages over a period of time. Common size analysis is of immense use for comparing enterprises which differ substantially in size as it provides an insight into the structure of financial statements. Inter-firm comparison or comparison of the company’s position with the related industry as a whole is possible with the help of common size statement analysis. body:
A company issues shares for cash and collects the amount in four separate instalments: application money, allotment money, a first call and a final call. The calls are made successively, with the first call preceding the final call. Arrange the instalments in chronological order.
(A) Application money
(B) Allotment money
(C) First call money
(D) Final call money
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The stages for collecting share money are application, allotment and call or calls, in that order. Since the stem states that the first call precedes the final call, the sequence is (A)-(B)-(C)-(D).

Issue of Shares for Consideration Other than Cash Summary Company: An organisation consisting of individuals called ‘shareholders’ by virtue of their holding the shares of a company, who can act as legal person as regards its business through board of directors. Share: Fractional part of the capital, and forms the basis of ownership in a company. Shares are generally of two types, viz. equity shares and preference shares, according to the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013. Preference shares again are of different types based on varying shades of rights attached to them. Share Capital of a company is collected by issuing shares to either a select group of persons through the route of private placements and/or offered to the public for subscription. Thus, the issue of shares is basic to the capital of a company. Shares are issued either for cash or for consideration other than cash, the former being more common. Shares are said to be issued for consideration other than cash when a company purchases business, or some asset/assets, and the vendors have agreed to receive payment in the form of fully paid shares of a company. Stages of Share Issue: The issue of shares for cash is required to be made in strict conformity with the procedure laid down by law for the same. When shares are issued for cash, the amount on them can be collected at one or more of the following stages: (i) Application for shares (ii) Allotment of shares (iii) Call/Calls on shares. body: A company records the following cash transactions during one accounting period: it receives ₹2,40,000 from the sale of machinery, collects ₹1,10,000 from trade receivables, pays ₹1,80,000 in cash to purchase machinery, pays ₹70,000 to employees, and pays ₹90,000 to purchase marketable securities that constitute cash equivalents. These are the only transactions considered. What is the net cash inflow from these transactions to be reflected in the cash flow statement?
options: ["₹1,00,000 net cash inflow","₹10,000 net cash inflow","₹2,80,000 net cash inflow","₹4,60,000 net cash inflow"]
explanation: The purchase of marketable securities is excluded because the stem states that they constitute cash equivalents. The counted inflows total ₹3,50,000, and the counted outflows total ₹2,50,000. Therefore, the net cash inflow is ₹1,00,000.

body:
Match each buy-back circumstance in List-I with the corresponding implication in List-II. Assess only the feature stated in each entry.

List-I
(A) Shares to be bought back are purchased from the open market.
(B) The buy-back is made out of free reserves.
(C) The buy-back is completed 10 months after the date of passing the special resolution.
(D) Shares selected for buy-back are not fully paid-up.

List-II
(I) This is a stated source from which a company may buy back its own shares.
(II) An amount equal to the nominal value of shares bought back must be transferred to the Capital Redemption Reserve Account.
(III) Completion occurs within 12 months from the date of passing the special resolution.
(IV) The stated requirement that shares bought back be fully paid-up is not met.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The open market is a stated source for buying back shares, and a buy-back out of free reserves requires a transfer equal to the nominal value of the shares bought back to the Capital Redemption Reserve Account. Completion 10 months after the special resolution falls within the 12-month period, while shares bought back must be fully paid-up.

body:
Consider the following statements about the bases used in common-size statements:
(A) In a common-size balance sheet, each asset is expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(B) In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations.
(C) In a common-size balance sheet, each asset is expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations.
(D) In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of total assets.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(A) and (B) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: A common-size balance sheet expresses each asset as a percentage of total assets, while a common-size statement of profit and loss expresses expenditure items as a percentage of revenue from operations. Therefore, statements (A) and (B) are correct; (C) and (D) reverse the respective bases.

body: A firm values goodwill using the Average Profits Method. Its profits for the three past years were ₹36,000, ₹48,000 and ₹60,000. Calculate average past profit as the arithmetic mean of these three profits, and use an agreed three years’ purchase. What is the goodwill value?
explanation: Average past profit is (₹36,000 + ₹48,000 + ₹60,000) ÷ 3 = ₹48,000. Goodwill is the average past profit multiplied by the agreed three years’ purchase: ₹48,000 × 3 = ₹1,44,000.

body: A new partner brings a goodwill premium of ₹1,20,000 through the firm. The firm credits the premium to the new partner’s capital account and then adjusts it in favour of the two sacrificing partners, A and B, in their sacrifice ratio of 3:2. A and B each withdraw one-quarter of the amount credited to their respective capital accounts. No other adjustment affects A’s capital account. What amount of this premium remains credited to A’s capital account after the withdrawal?
explanation: A’s share of the premium is ₹1,20,000 × 3/5 = ₹72,000, since the premium is distributed in the sacrificing ratio. A withdraws one-quarter of that amount, or ₹18,000. Therefore, ₹54,000 remains credited to A’s capital account.

body: A firm is calculating the amount due to the executor of a deceased partner. All amounts below are already the deceased partner’s attributable amounts, in rupees, and the partner has not yet been paid. The partner’s capital account has a credit balance of ₹1,50,000 and the current account has a credit balance of ₹8,000. The partner’s share of goodwill is ₹25,000, accumulated profits are ₹12,000, and the gain on revaluation is ₹5,000. The partner’s share of profit up to death is ₹15,000; interest on capital due up to death is ₹3,000; and salary due up to death is ₹2,000. The partner’s share of accumulated losses is ₹6,000, and drawings to be deducted are ₹9,000. There are no other credits or deductions. What amount is due to the executor?
explanation: The stated credits total ₹2,20,000. The deductions are ₹6,000 + ₹9,000 = ₹15,000, so the amount due is ₹2,20,000 − ₹15,000 = ₹2,05,000.

body:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Method characterised by disclosure of major classes of gross cash receipts and gross cash payments
(B) Method characterised by adjustment of net profit or loss for the specified effects
(C) Starting point under the indirect method
(D) Statement about the availability under the indirect method of information useful in estimating future cash flows

List-II
(I) Direct method
(II) Adjustment of net profit or loss for non-cash transactions, deferrals or accruals of operating cash receipts, and income or expenses associated with investing or financing cash flows
(III) Net profit or loss before taxation and extraordinary items
(IV) Information useful in estimating future cash flows is not available under the indirect method

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The direct method discloses major classes of gross cash receipts and payments, while the indirect method adjusts net profit or loss for the specified effects. The indirect method starts with net profit or loss before taxation and extraordinary items. Information useful in estimating future cash flows is not available under the indirect method.

As per AS-3, ‘Cash’ comprises cash in hand and demand deposits with banks, and ‘Cash equivalents’ means short-term highly liquid investments that are readily convertible into known amounts of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value. An investment normally qualifies as cash equivalents only when it has a short maturity, of say, three months or less from the date of acquisition. Investments in shares are excluded from cash equivalents unless they are in substantial cash equivalents. For example, preference shares of a company acquired shortly before their specific redemption date, provided there is only insignificant risk of failure of the company to repay the amount at maturity. Similarly, short-term marketable securities which can be readily converted into cash are treated as cash equivalents and is liquidable immediately without considerable change in value. 6.4 Cash Flows ‘Cash Flows’ implies movement of cash in and out due to some non-cash items. Receipt of cash from a non-cash item is termed as cash inflow while cash payment in respect of such items as cash outflow. For example, purchase of machinery by paying cash is cash outflow while sale proceeds received from sale of machinery is cash inflow. Other examples of cash flows include collection of cash from trade receivables, payment to trade payables, payment to employees, receipt of dividend, interest payments, etc. Cash management includes the investment of excess cash in cash equivalents.","url":"https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/leac206.pdf","publisher":"NCERT","title":"Cash Flow Statement","kind":"reference"}]

body:
A company issues debentures and creates a charge on a specific machine held for use in its operations and not meant for sale. The charge is for payment in case of default. Which of the following statements are correct?

(A) The charge is a fixed charge.
(B) The charge is a floating charge.
(C) The debentures are secured debentures.
(D) A fixed charge is created on the company's general assets.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(A) and (D) only","(B) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only"]
explanation: A fixed charge is created on a specific asset held for use in operations and not meant for sale, so the charge on the machine is fixed. A charge on assets for payment in case of default makes the debentures secured. A floating charge is on general assets, not the specified machine.

body:
A company is preparing common-size balance sheets for two years. Arrange the following steps in the order it should follow:
(A) Calculate each asset item's percentage of total assets for each year.
(B) List the absolute rupee figures for the two years.
(C) Take total assets as the common base of 100.

explanation: First, list the absolute figures for the two years. Next, choose the common base; for a balance sheet, total assets is an appropriate base. Then calculate each asset item's percentage of that total for each year.

body: Before D is admitted, A, B and C share profits in the ratio 7:5:4. The partners and D agree that D will receive 3/10 of the firm’s total profits. This share is acquired by taking 1/10 of the total profits from A, 1/12 from B, and the balance of D’s share from C. What is the new profit-sharing ratio A:B:C:D?
explanation: The old shares are A = 7/16, B = 5/16 and C = 4/16. D’s remaining share taken from C is 3/10 − 1/10 − 1/12 = 7/60, so the new shares are A = 7/16 − 1/10 = 27/80, B = 5/16 − 1/12 = 11/48, C = 1/4 − 7/60 = 2/15, and D = 3/10. Expressed with denominator 240, these shares give the ratio 81:55:32:72.

body: A firm presents its balance sheets for two periods in comparative form. It applied one accounting principle differently in the two periods. What should it do about this difference?
options: ["Identify the analysis as vertical analysis.","Mention the deviation in the use of accounting principles in a footnote.","Express each item as a percentage of a common item.","Treat the figures as comparable solely because two periods are displayed side by side."]
explanation: Comparative figures are comparable only when the same accounting principles are used in preparing the statements. When a principle differs, the deviation should be mentioned in a footnote.

Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector. 4.4 Tools of Analysis of Financial Statements The most commonly used techniques of financial analysis are as follows: 1. Comparative Statements: These are the statements showing the profitability and financial position of a firm for different periods of time in a comparative form to give an idea about the position of two or more periods. It usually applies to the two important financial statements, namely, balance sheet and statement of profit and loss prepared in a comparative form. The financial data will be comparative only when same accounting principles are used in preparing these statements. If this is not the case, the deviation in the use of accounting principles should be mentioned as a footnote. Comparative figures indicate the trend and direction of financial position and operating results. This analysis is also known as ‘horizontal analysis’. 2. Common Size Statements: These are the statements which indicate the relationship of different items of a financial statement with a common item by expressing each item as a percentage of that common item. The percentage thus calculated can be easily compared with the results of corresponding percentages of the previous year or of some other firms, as the numbers are brought to common base. Such statements also allow an analyst to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry. Thus, common size statements are useful, both, in intra-firm comparisons over different years and also in making inter-firm comparisons for the same year or for several years. body: A company has 24,000 allotted shares, and the second and final call of ₹18 per share is due on every share. Calls in advance of ₹72,000 have already been received and are available in full to adjust against this call. The remaining call money is received in full in cash on the due date, with no other receipts or deductions. How much cash does the company receive on the due date?
explanation: The total call due is 24,000 × ₹18 = ₹4,32,000. The ₹72,000 received in advance is adjusted against the call, so the company receives ₹4,32,000 − ₹72,000 = ₹3,60,000 in cash on the due date.

body:
Match each case in List-I with the inference in List-II.
List-I
(A) A firm obtains goodwill values of ₹2,40,000 and ₹2,70,000 using two different valuation methods.
(B) The existing partners and the incoming partner are considering how to settle which valuation method will be used.
(C) The item being valued is goodwill, an intangible asset.
(D) The firm is considering Average Profits, Super Profits and Capitalisation as valuation methods.
List-II
(I) The method of valuation may be specifically decided between the existing and incoming partners.
(II) Goodwill calculated by one method may differ from that calculated by another method.
(III) Accurate calculation of goodwill is difficult.
(IV) More than one method is available for valuing goodwill.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The different values in (A) match the possibility that goodwill calculated by different methods may differ, while (B) concerns specifically deciding which method to use. Goodwill’s intangible nature makes accurate valuation difficult, and the three named approaches show that more than one method is available.

body:
During the year, Company X pays a cash instalment on a fixed asset acquired on a deferred payment basis. The instalment comprises an interest element and a loan element. Which statements correctly classify these two cash-flow elements?
(A) The interest element is classified under financing activities.
(B) The loan element is classified under investing activities.
(C) The interest element is classified under investing activities.
(D) The loan element is classified under financing activities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (D) only","(B) and (C) only","(A) and (B) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: The instalment contains two elements that are classified differently: the interest element is a financing activity, while the loan element is an investing activity. Therefore, statements (A) and (B) are correct.

Separate disclosure of cash flows arising from financing activities is important because it is useful in predicting claims on future cash flows by providers of funds ( both capital and borrowings ) to the enterprise. Examples of financing activities are: Cash Inflows from financing activities  Cash proceeds from issuing shares (equity or/and preference).  Cash proceeds from issuing debentures, loans, bonds and other short/ long-term borrowings. A deceased partner’s share of profit for an intervening period is to be estimated using the preceding year’s profit. The preceding year’s profit is ₹2,40,000, the intervening period is three months of a 12-month year, and the deceased partner’s share is 1/4. Arrange the following steps in the order needed to estimate the deceased partner’s share.
(A) Apply the deceased partner’s 1/4 share to the firm’s estimated profit for the three-month period.
(B) Divide the annual profit base established in (D) by 12 to obtain the monthly estimate.
(C) Multiply the monthly estimate from (B) by 3 to estimate the firm’s profit for the intervening period.
(D) Take the preceding year’s profit, ₹2,40,000, as the annual profit base.
explanation: First use ₹2,40,000 as the annual base, then divide by 12 and multiply by 3 to estimate the firm’s profit for the intervening period: ₹60,000. Applying the deceased partner’s 1/4 share gives ₹15,000, so the steps are (D), (B), (C), (A).

body:
Two companies have the following balance-sheet figures. All amounts are in rupees.
Company P: Year 1—total assets ₹8,00,000, inventories ₹1,60,000, cash and cash equivalents ₹80,000; Year 2—total assets ₹10,00,000, inventories ₹2,00,000, cash and cash equivalents ₹1,00,000.
Company Q: Year 1—total assets ₹20,00,000, inventories ₹4,00,000, cash and cash equivalents ₹3,00,000; Year 2—total assets ₹25,00,000, inventories ₹5,00,000, cash and cash equivalents ₹2,50,000.
For each company and year, calculate each listed asset item as a percentage of that year's total assets. Which conclusion is correct?
options: ["The comparison uses Year 1 total assets as the base for both years, so each company's inventory share rises from 20% to 25%.","Inventory shares remain 20% for both companies in both years; P's cash share remains 10%, while Q's falls from 15% to 10%.","Inventory shares remain 20% for both companies in both years; P's cash share remains 10%, while Q's rises from 10% to 15%.","Revenue from operations is the common base for these balance-sheet items, so the asset figures cannot establish their common-size percentages."]
explanation: For a common-size balance sheet, each asset item's percentage is calculated using the total assets for the same year as the base. Inventories are 20% of total assets in all four company-year cases; P's cash shares are 10% in both years, while Q's are 15% in Year 1 and 10% in Year 2. Thus, option B is correct.

Here, each item in the statement is stated as a percentage of the aggregate, or revenue from operations of which that item is a part. For example, a common size balance sheet shows the percentage of each asset to the total assets, and that of each liability to the total liabilities. Similarly, in the common size statement of profit and loss, the items of expenditure are shown as a percentage of the revenue from operations. If such a statement is prepared for successive periods, it shows the changes of the respective percentages over a period of time. Common size analysis is of immense use for comparing enterprises which differ substantially in size as it provides an insight into the structure of financial statements. body: A firm has prepared its Profit and Loss A/c, which shows a net profit. Its partnership terms provide for a partner’s salary and interest on capital, and the firm needs to record these adjustments and show how the profit is appropriated among the partners. Which account should it use?
options: ["Profit and Loss A/c","Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c","Interest on Capital A/c","Partners’ Capital/Current A/cs"]
explanation: The Profit and Loss Appropriation Account is an extension of the Profit and Loss Account and shows how profits are distributed among partners. The specified partner-related adjustments are made through it. The Profit and Loss A/c in the stem has already provided the net profit.

body: Asha is considering four separate purchases of shares. Company Z is the issuer of the shares, Ravi is an investor who holds shares, and the named seller in each option is the actual seller. Which purchase is in the secondary market?
options: ["Asha purchases shares from Company Z in a fresh issue.","Asha purchases shares from Ravi, an investor who already holds them.","Asha purchases shares from Company Z, which is selling shares it previously issued.","Asha purchases shares from Company Z through a broker; Company Z is the seller."]
explanation: A secondary market transaction is one in which an investor buys or sells shares or securities from another investor rather than from the issuer. Ravi is an investor who holds the shares, so Asha’s purchase from him is in the secondary market. In the other options, Company Z, the issuer, is the stated seller.

topic: Financial Markets: focus on this supplied section: One of the main objectives of the primary market is to allow companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
A company plans to raise capital by issuing securities in a primary-market transaction. Consider the following statements about the objective served by this plan:
(A) The plan uses a route through which the primary market allows companies to raise capital.
(B) In the objective described, the company is the capital-raising party.
(C) The objective described is to enable investors, rather than companies, to raise capital through securities issuance.
(D) Under the objective described, the company raises capital without issuing securities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (C) only","(A) and (D) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: The plan matches the objective: the primary market allows companies to raise capital through securities issuance, so both (A) and (B) follow. Statement (C) changes the capital-raising party, while (D) removes the securities-issuance route described.

body:
Company K is the issuer of a security. Riya, Kabir, Meera and Omar are investors. The following transfers of the same security are listed in shuffled order. There were no other transfers, and each seller must first acquire the security before transferring it.
(A) Kabir transfers the security to Meera.
(B) Company K transfers the security to Riya.
(C) Meera transfers the security to Omar.
(D) Riya transfers the security to Kabir.
Arrange the transfers from earliest to latest, beginning with the issuer’s transfer and ending with Omar’s acquisition.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Company K must transfer the security to Riya first. Riya then transfers it to Kabir, Kabir to Meera, and Meera to Omar. The transfers after the issuer’s transfer are between investors, as described in the definition of the secondary market.

body: A company is considering an expansion. Workstream X compares the costs and benefits of the available investment and financing alternatives and recommends one with the objective of increasing shareholders’ wealth. Once that decision is made, Workstream Y forecasts which items are likely to change as operations expand, estimates the resulting fund requirements in amount and timing, and anticipates shortages or surpluses so that action can be taken in advance to support smooth operations. Which classification correctly identifies X and Y, respectively?
options: ["Workstream X: Financial planning; Workstream Y: Financial management","Workstream X: Financial management; Workstream Y: Financial management","Workstream X: Financial planning; Workstream Y: Financial planning","Workstream X: Financial management; Workstream Y: Financial planning"]
explanation: Workstream X selects investment and financing alternatives by considering costs and benefits, with the objective of increasing shareholders’ wealth; this is financial management. Workstream Y forecasts changing fund requirements in both amount and timing and anticipates shortages or surpluses to support smooth operations; this is financial planning. Therefore, option D correctly classifies both workstreams.

Financial Planning Financial planning is essentially the preparation of a financial blueprint of an organisation’s future operations. The objective of financial planning is to ensure that enough funds are available at right time. If adequate funds are not available the firm will not be able to honour its commitments and carry out its plans. On the other hand, if excess funds are available, it will unnecessarily add to the cost and may encourage wasteful expenditure. It must be kept in mind that financial planning is not equivalent to, or a substitute for, financial management. Financial management aims at choosing the best investment and financing alternatives by focusing on their costs and benefits. Its objective is to increase the shareholders’ wealth. Financial planning on the other hand aims at smooth operations by focusing on fund requirements and their availability in the light of financial decisions. For example, if a capital budgeting decisions is taken, the operations are likely to be at a higher scale. The amount of expenses and revenues are likely to increase. Financial planning process tries to forecast all the items which are likely to undergo changes. It enables the management to foresee the fund requirements both the quantum as well as the timing. Likely shortage and surpluses are forecast so that necessary activities are taken in advance to meet those situations. Thus, financial planning strives to achieve the following twin objectives. (a) To ensure availability of funds whenever requir ed: This include a proper estimation of the funds required for different purposes such as for the purchase of long- term assets or to meet day-to- day expenses of business etc. Apart from this, there is a need to estimate the time at which these funds are to be made available. Financial planning also tries to specify possible sources of these funds. (b) To see tha t the firm does not raise resources unnecessarily: Excess funding is almost as bad as inadequate funding. Even if there is some surplus money, good financial planning would put it to the best possible use so that the financial resources are not left idle and don’t unnecessarily add to the cost. Thus, a proper matching of funds requirements and their availability is sought to be achieved by financial planning. A company has a department manager who guides her subordinates and posts designated as supervisor in its organisational hierarchy. Consider the following statements:
(A) The department manager's guidance of her subordinates can be supervision as an element of directing.
(B) Supervision as an element of directing is performed only by employees whose posts are designated as supervisors.
(C) Supervision can also denote a function performed by supervisors in the organisational hierarchy.
(D) As an element of directing, supervision concerns monitoring completed work; giving instructions is excluded.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A), (C) only","(A), (D) only","(B), (C) only","(B), (D) only"]
explanation: The department manager is a manager with subordinates, so guiding their efforts can be supervision as an element of directing. Supervision can also refer to a function performed by supervisors in the organisational hierarchy. Giving instructions is included in the description of supervision, so statement (D) is incorrect.

List-I
(A) Government officials express a favourable attitude towards business, without issuing a formal direction.

body:
The stages below describe one company’s single capital-raising episode. Arrange them from the initial aim to the completed outcome.
(A) The company seeks to raise capital.
(B) The company issues securities in the primary market.
(C) The company raises capital through the issuance.
Choose the correct sequence from the options below:
explanation: The company’s aim to raise capital comes first, followed by issuing securities in the primary market. The stated outcome is that capital is raised through that issuance, so it follows the issue of securities.

body:
Four firms propose investing procured funds as follows. For every firm, the procurement cost and expected investment return are annual percentages calculated on the same basis, and no other costs or returns affect the comparison.
Firm P: procurement cost 8%; expected return 7%.
Firm Q: procurement cost 9%; expected return 9%.
Firm R: procurement cost 10%; expected return 11%.
Firm S: procurement cost 12%; expected return 11%.
Which firm's proposal satisfies the requirement that the return from procured finance exceed its procurement cost?
options: ["Firm R only","Firm Q only","Firm P only","Firm S only"]
explanation: The return must be greater than, not merely equal to, the cost of procuring the funds. Firm R's 11% expected return exceeds its 10% procurement cost; P and S have returns below cost, while Q's return equals its cost.

body: A distribution firm introduces a needed change to its order-routing procedure. The dispatch team initially resists. The manager uses communication, leadership and motivation; the team then accepts the change and cooperates in introducing it. The case states that cooperation and commitment among other groups have not developed and balance among departments has not yet been achieved. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: ["The team's acceptance establishes organisational stability and balance, even though other groups lack cooperation and departmental balance remains unachieved.","The manager's directing can reduce resistance and develop cooperation in introducing the change, but this case does not establish wider stability and balance.","The team's initial resistance makes the needed change unworkable, even when the manager uses directing to develop cooperation in its introduction.","The manager used motivation alone, so communication and leadership played no part in reducing resistance or developing cooperation."]
explanation: Effective directing helps reduce resistance and develop cooperation for introducing needed change, which fits the dispatch team's response. The case does not establish wider stability and balance: it states that wider cooperation and commitment and departmental balance have not been achieved, while stability and balance are linked to cooperation and commitment among people and balance across groups, activities and departments. A contradicts the stated case, C contradicts the stated role of directing, and D contradicts the stated use of communication and leadership.

body:
Match each situation in List-I with the most directly relevant distribution responsibility in List-II. Treat each situation as a separate issue, and use each entry in List-II once.

List-I
(A) A customer seeks a product at a retail outlet, but it is unavailable there and the customer may buy an alternative brand.
(B) Production is seasonal, while the sale or use of the goods occurs later, creating a time gap.
(C) Users are widely spread and geographically separated from the place of production.
(D) The firm must decide whether to use wholesalers, retailers, or both as intermediaries.

List-II
(I) Moving goods to the place where they are needed for consumption or use
(II) Storing goods to maintain a smooth flow between production or procurement and sale or use
(III) Selecting channels of distribution
(IV) Making goods physically available where customers want to buy them

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The unavailable product concerns making goods physically available where customers want to buy them, while a time gap caused by seasonal production calls for storage. Geographic separation calls for moving goods to where they are needed, and choosing wholesalers or retailers is a channel decision. Thus, the correct mapping is (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

body:
A business is preparing a management note. Arrange the following statements from the overall purpose of resource use, to the basic objective, to the objective beyond mere survival, and finally to the long-run objective.
(A) Management seeks profit, which is essential for covering costs and business risks.
(B) Management aims to use human and material resources to maximum possible advantage to fulfil the business’s economic objectives.
(C) Management seeks enough revenue to cover costs so that the organisation survives.
(D) Management exploits the organisation’s growth potential for long-run prospects.
Choose the correct sequence from the options below:
explanation: The overall purpose is to use human and material resources to maximum advantage in fulfilling economic objectives. Survival is the basic objective; mere survival is not enough, so profit is also required. Growth is the long-run objective, giving the sequence (B), (C), (A), (D).

body: Which of the following is named as a principle of Taylor’s scientific management?
options: ["Functional foremanship","Science, not the rule of thumb","Division of work","Unity of command"]
explanation: “Science, not the rule of thumb” is named among Taylor’s principles of scientific management. Functional foremanship is listed as a Taylor technique, while Division of work and Unity of command are listed among Fayol’s principles.

The significance can be discussed under the following heads- Increase in efficiency; Optimum utilisation of resources; Scientific decision making; Adaptation to changing environment; Fulfilling social responsibilities; Proper research and development; Training managers; and Effective administration. Scientific Management Taylor’s principles of scientific management are — Science, not the rule of thumb; Harmony not discord; Cooperation not individualism; Maximum not restricted output; Development of each person to her/ his greatest efficiency and prosperity. The techniques of scientific management as per Taylor were — Functional foremanship; Standardisation and simplification of work; Fatigue Study; Method Study; Time Study; Motion Study; and Differential Wage System. We can also point out differences between the contributions of Taylor and Fayol but essentially they were complementary in nature. Fayol’s Principles of Management According to Fayol, the functions of management are to plan, to organise, to command, to coordinate and to control. The activities of an industrial undertaking could be divided into; Technical; Commercial; Financial; Security; Accounting and Managerial. He also suggested that managers should have the following qualities- Physical; Moral; Education; Knowledge; and Experience. body: A student is classifying four share transactions. In each option, the named parties are the parties directly involved. Which transaction takes place in the secondary market?
options: ["Nisha buys shares directly from the company that issued them.","Nisha sells shares directly to the company that issued them.","Nisha buys shares directly from Kabir, another investor.","Nisha receives shares from Kabir as a gift, with no purchase or sale."]
explanation: A secondary market transaction is a purchase or sale of shares or securities between investors, rather than a transaction with the issuer. In option C, Nisha buys shares from Kabir, who is identified as another investor. In A and B, the company that issued the shares is the other party; D involves no purchase or sale.

body:
Consider two situations. In each, a manager guides and counsels staff, motivates them and leads their efforts. In Case X, these actions are directed towards an organisational objective. In Case Y, their sole intended aim is the manager’s personal objective, expressly unrelated to any organisational objective. Which statements are correct?
(A) Case X is consistent with directing because the actions are used to lead people towards an organisational objective.
(B) Case Y is necessarily directing too, because using these actions is sufficient regardless of the intended objective.
(C) Case X is not merely communication, since motivation and leadership are among the elements encompassed by directing.
(D) In Case X, guiding and counselling fall outside directing; only motivation and leadership can be part of it.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(B) and (D) only","(C) and (D) only","(A) and (C) only"]
explanation: Case X fits the stated meaning because the manager uses the described actions to lead people towards an organisational objective. Directing includes guiding, counselling, motivating and leading, and is not merely communication. Case Y’s aim is expressly unrelated to an organisational objective, while D wrongly excludes guiding and counselling from directing.

You can observe here that directing is not a mere issue of communication but encompasses many elements like supervision, motivation and leadership. It is one of the key managerial functions performed by every manager. Directing is a managerial process which takes place throughout the life of an organisation. The main characteristics of directing are discussed below: (i) Directing initiates action: Directing is a key managerial function. A manager has to perform this function along with planning, organising, staffing and controlling while discharging his duties in the organisation. While other functions prepare a setting for action, directing initiates action in the organisation. (ii) Directing takes place at every level of management: Every manager, from top executive to supervisor performs the function of directing. The directing takes place wherever superior – subordinate relations exist. (iii) Directing is a continuous process: Directing is a continuous activity. It takes place throughout the life of the organisation irrespective of people occupying managerial positions. We can observe that in organisations like Infosys, Tata, BHEL, HLL and the managers may change but the directing process continues because without direction the organisational activities can not continue further. (iv) Directing flows from top to bottom: Directing is first initiated at top level and flows to the bottom through organisational hierarchy.","url":"https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebs107.pdf","publisher":"NCERT","title":"NCERT Business Studies I, Chapter 7: Directing, reprint 2026–27","kind":"reference"},{"id":"ncert-lebs107","locator":"normative-34f28c2e46790f5a","text":"For example, a good motivation plan with suitable monetary and non-monetary rewards can motivate an employee to contribute his maximum efforts for the organisation as he or she may feel that their efforts will bring them suitable rewards. (ii) Harmony of objectives: Very often, we find that individual objectives of employees and the organisational objectives as understood are conflicting to each other. For example, an employee may expect attractive salary and monetary benefits to fulfill his personal needs. The organisation may expect employees to improve productivity to achieve expected profits. But, good directing should provide harmony by convincing that employee rewards and work efficiency are complimentary to each other. (iii) Unity of Command: This principle insists that a person in the organisation should receive instructions from one superior only. If instructions are received from more than one, it creates confusion, conflict and disorder in the organisation. Adherence to this principle ensures effective direction. (iv) Appropriateness of direction tech­ nique: According to this principle, appropriate motivational and leadership technique should be used while directing the people based on subordinate needs, capabilities, attitudes and other situational variables. For example, for some people money can act as powerful motivator while for others promotion may act as effective motivator. (v) Managerial communication: Effe- ctive managerial communication across all the levels in the organisation makes direction effective. Directing should convey clear instructions to create total understanding to subordinates.","url":"https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebs107.pdf","publisher":"NCERT","title":"NCERT Business Studies I, Chapter 7: Directing, reprint 2026–27","kind":"reference"}]

Match each recruitment source in List-I with its described feature in List-II.
List-I
(A) Campus recruitment
(B) Recommendations of employees
(C) Labour contractors
(D) Web publishing
List-II
(I) Websites provide information about job seekers and job openings and are visited by prospective employees and organisations.
(II) Contractors can supply the required number of unskilled workers at short notice.
(III) Recruitment from educational institutions for various jobs.
(IV) Applicants introduced by present employees, or their friends and relatives, whose background is sufficiently known.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Campus recruitment refers to recruiting from educational institutions, while employee recommendations involve applicants introduced by present employees or their friends and relatives. Labour contractors can provide unskilled workers at short notice, and web publishing provides information about job seekers and job openings through websites.

body: A firm's projected cash remaining after normal business operations and planned fixed-asset investment is ₹12,00,000 for the coming quarter. Interest and principal payments on its existing debt for that quarter total ₹12,00,000. A proposed loan would add ₹2,00,000 of interest and principal payments due in the same quarter. Assume the loan proceeds are fully committed to the asset project and cannot be used for debt service, and no other cash inflow or reserve is available. Which assessment is best supported by the projected cash-flow position?
options: ["The projection supports the loan because it covers existing interest and principal payments.","The projection supports the loan because fixed-asset spending is excluded from cash obligations.","The projection does not support the loan because total debt service exceeds cash available and no buffer remains.","The projection supports the loan because only interest, not principal repayment, counts as debt service."]
explanation: The projected ₹12,00,000 is fully required for existing debt service, and the proposed loan adds ₹2,00,000 of payments. Total debt service would therefore be ₹14,00,000 against ₹12,00,000 of projected cash, leaving a shortfall and no buffer. The stated assumption that loan proceeds cannot be used for debt service means they do not cover that shortfall.

body: A manufacturing unit has set a permissible limit for machine downtime in a key result area designated as critical. In one shift, downtime exceeds that limit, and the deviation is brought to the manager’s notice. No investigation has yet established its cause. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: ["Analyse possible causes of the deviation before deciding a response.","Treat the deviation as proof that the standard was unrealistic and revise it immediately.","Treat the deviation as proof that employees lacked effort and issue a warning.","Classify the deviation as a routine problem and leave it to subordinates without further managerial analysis."]
explanation: The deviation has crossed the permissible limit and has been brought to the manager’s attention. The stated principle is to analyse deviations that demand managerial attention for their causes; the cause should not be assumed because deviations may have multiple possible causes.

body:
Two firms sell the same physical refrigerator model. Firm P also provides after-sales service, handles complaints and makes spare parts available; Firm Q offers none of these. Assume these are the only differences in their offers. Consider the following statements:
(A) The firms’ product offers are necessarily identical because their physical refrigerators are identical.
(B) Firm P’s after-sales service, complaint handling and spare-part availability may form part of the extended product.
(C) The firms’ total product offers may differ even though their physical refrigerators are identical.
(D) Support provided after purchase is outside the concept of product.
Which statements are correct?
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(B) and (C) only"]
explanation: The concept of product includes more than the physical item: it can include benefits to customers and an extended product, such as after-sales service, complaint handling and spare-part availability. Therefore, Firm P’s support may make its total product offer different from Firm Q’s, even though the physical refrigerators are identical. Statements (A) and (D) incorrectly exclude these aspects from the product concept.

body:
Match each description in List-I with the delegation element or condition in List-II.
List-I
(A) A right derived from formal position to direct a subordinate within the scope of the job
(B) An obligation to perform an assigned duty, arising from delegated authority
(C) Answerability for the outcome of an assigned task, arising from responsibility
(D) The authority granted for a job is aligned with the responsibility assigned for it
List-II
(I) Accountability
(II) Authority
(III) Commensurateness of authority with responsibility
(IV) Responsibility
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Authority is the right to command and arises from formal position, while responsibility is the obligation to perform an assigned task and arises from delegated authority. Accountability is answerability for the task’s outcome and arises from responsibility. Effective delegation also requires the authority granted to be commensurate with the assigned responsibility.

(A) The National Commission issues its order on the appeal.
(B) The State Commission issues its order.

(D) An appeal is filed with the National Commission against the State Commission’s order.

explanation: The State Commission must issue its order before an appeal against it is filed with the National Commission. The National Commission then issues its order, which is followed by the appeal to the Supreme Court.

body: Which comparison provides the nutritional-value basis for associating organically grown food with healthy food?
options: ["It has more nutritional value than food from chemical farming.","It requires less labour input than conventional farming.","It is sold at a lower price than conventional food.","It involves greater pesticide use than conventional farming."]
explanation: Organically grown food is stated to have more nutritional value than food from chemical farming, thereby providing healthy foods. The other choices conflict with the stated higher labour requirement, higher price and pesticide-free nature of organic produce.

body: A groundwater resource is replenished at a constant rate of 32 lakh litres per month. Over a three-month period, existing users will withdraw 43 lakh litres in total. A proposed project requests a further 58 lakh litres during the same period; these are the only withdrawals. For this calculation, apply only the condition that total resource extraction over the period must not exceed regeneration over that period. By how much does the proposed withdrawal exceed the maximum additional withdrawal consistent with this condition?
options: ["15 lakh litres","38 lakh litres","53 lakh litres","5 lakh litres"]
explanation: Regeneration over three months is 32 × 3 = 96 lakh litres. After the existing withdrawals of 43 lakh litres, the maximum additional withdrawal is 96 − 43 = 53 lakh litres. The proposed withdrawal exceeds this amount by 58 − 53 = 5 lakh litres.

Match List-I with List-II. Assume all transactions described concern residents of a country and the rest of the world. In (C), the transaction is expressly identified as factor income or non-factor income.
List-I
(A) The account that records trade in goods and services and transfer payments
(B) A resident's export or import of a good
(C) A cross-border transaction identified as factor income or non-factor income
(D) A resident receives a gift from abroad without supplying any good or service in return
List-II
(I) Transfer payments
(II) Current Account
(III) Trade in goods
(IV) Trade in services
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A. (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
B. (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
C. (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
D. (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
explanation: The Current Account records trade in goods and services and transfer payments. Exports and imports are trade in goods, while factor-income and non-factor-income transactions are trade in services. A gift received without providing goods or services in return is a transfer payment.

In other words, the currency will maintain a stable purchasing power. Without this confidence, a currency will not be used as an international medium of exchange and unit of account since there is no international authority with the power to force the use of a particular currency in international transactions. In the past, governments have tried to gain confidence of potential users by announcing that the national currency will be freely convertible at a fixed price into another asset. Also, the issuing authority will have no control over the value of that asset into which the currency can be converted. This other asset most often has been gold, or other national currencies. There are two aspects of this commitment that has affected its credibility — the ability to convert freely in unlimited amounts and the price at which this conversion takes place. The international monetary system has been set up to handle these issues and ensure stability in international transactions. With the increase in the volume of transactions, gold ceased to be the asset into which national currencies could be converted (See Box 6.2). Although some national currencies have international acceptability, what is important in transactions between two countries is the currency in which the trade occurs. For instance, if an Indian wants to buy a good made in America, she would need dollars to complete the transaction. If the price of the good is ten dollars, she would need to know how much it would cost her in Indian rupees. That is, she will need to know the price of dollar in terms of rupees. The price of one currency in terms of another currency is known as the foreign exchange rate or simply the exchange rate . We will discuss this in detail in section 6.2. 6.1 THE BALANCE OF PAYMENTS The balance of payments (BoP) record the transactions in goods, services and assets between residents of a country with the rest of the world for a specified time period typically a year. There are two main accounts in the BoP — the current account and the capital account1. 6.1.1 Current Account Current Account is the record of trade in goods and services and transfer payments. Figure 6.1 illustrates the components of Current Account. Trade in goods includes exports and imports of goods. Trade in services includes factor income and non-factor income transactions. Transfer payments are the receipts which the residents of a country get for ‘free’, without having to provide any goods or services in return. They consist of gifts, remittances and grants. They could be given by the government or by private citizens living abroad. 1 There is a new classification in which the balance of payments have been divided into three accounts — the current account, the financial account and the capital account. This is as per the new accounting standards specified by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in the sixth edition of the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual (BPM6). India has also made the change but the Reserve Bank of India continues to publish data accounting to the old classification. A self-employed tailor has no hired workers. A non-farm casual wage labourer works for more than one employer. A private-sector establishment employs exactly 10 hired workers, and a separate public-sector establishment employs a worker. Consider the following statements:
(A) The tailor belongs to the informal sector.
(B) The non-farm casual wage labourer is included in the informal sector.
(C) Workers in the private-sector establishment belong to the formal sector.
(D) The worker in the public-sector establishment belongs to the informal sector.
Which statements are correct? Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A), (B) and (D) only","(A), (B) and (C) only","(A), (C) and (D) only","(B), (C) and (D) only"]
explanation: Statements (A) and (B) describe groups included in the informal sector: self-employed people without hired workers and non-farm casual wage labourers who work for more than one employer. A private-sector establishment with exactly 10 hired workers is formal, as are public-sector establishments. Therefore, only (A), (B) and (C) are correct.

body:
Arrange the following countries in chronological order according to the year in which reforms were introduced, from earliest to latest:
(A) India
(B) China
(C) Pakistan
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The reform years were 1978 for China, 1988 for Pakistan and 1991 for India. In ascending chronological order, the sequence is therefore China, Pakistan, India: (B), (C), (A).

Ø India, Pakistan and China have similar physical endowments but totally different political systems. Ø All the three countries follow the similar planned pattern of development. However, the structures established to implement developmental policies are quite different. Ø Till the early 1980s, the developmental indicators of all the three countries, such as growth rates and sectoral contribution towards national income, were similar. Ø Reforms were introduced in 1978 in China, in 1988 in Pakistan and in 1991 in India. Ø China introduced structural reforms on its own initiative while they were forced upon India and Pakistan by international agencies. Ø The impact of policy measures were different in these countries — for instance, one-child norm has arrested the population growth in China whereas in India and Pakistan, a major change is yet to take place. Ø Even after seventy years of planned development, majority of the workforce in all the countries depends on agriculture. The dependency is greater in India. Ø Though China has followed the classical development pattern of gradual shift from agriculture to manufacturing and then to services, India and Pakistan’s shift has been directly from agriculture to service sector. Ø China’s industrial sector has maintained a high growth rate while it is not so in both India and Pakistan. This led to rapid increase of the GDP per capita in China than in India and Pakistan. Ø China is ahead of India and Pakistan on many human development indicators. However these improvements were attributed not to the reform process but the strategies that China adopted in the pre-reform period. body: A village committee reviews a proposed paper mill that would use forest materials as industrial raw material. The mill is projected to employ 600 workers, and 1,200 residents use the same forest to meet daily needs. The government has allocated the forestland, but the proposal does not assess whether industrial use would restrict residents’ access; employment is its only quantified benefit. The industrialist argues that the job estimate and the allocation establish that the proposal is acceptable. Which response is best supported?
options: ["Reject the proposal solely because it involves industrial use of forest materials.","Assess whether residents’ daily needs would be deprived and weigh that impact alongside the employment offered.","Approve the proposal because its projected jobs establish that its benefits exceed its costs.","Treat the forestland allocation as evidence that residents’ daily needs are protected."]
explanation: The stated comparison makes the effect on people’s daily needs relevant when considering the employment offered by industrial use of forest materials. The proposal does not establish whether residents’ access would be restricted, so that impact must be assessed rather than treating the job estimate or land allocation as decisive.

body: A class must prepare lists of India’s major imported and exported items for 1990–91 and 2018–19, observe the differences, and discuss the impact of self-reliance. Which student plan completes this task?
options: ["Prepare lists of imports and exports for 1990–91 only, compare the two categories, and discuss self-reliance.","Prepare lists of imports and exports for both years, compare the lists, and discuss self-reliance.","Record changes in food-grain production and packaging technology, compare those changes, and discuss self-reliance.","Prepare lists of imports for both years only, compare the lists, and discuss self-reliance."]
explanation: The task requires lists of both imported and exported items for each year, followed by comparison and discussion of self-reliance. The second plan includes each of these steps. body:
An evaluator records four features of a rural women’s initiative. Match each feature in List-I with the corresponding purpose or outcome in List-II.

List-I
(A) Women receive training in latest agricultural techniques and organic farming.
(B) Women are encouraged to participate actively in raising agricultural productivity and family income.
(C) A Farm Women’s Group in Thiruchirapalli makes and sells vermicompost, earning money from the venture.
(D) Other Farm Women’s Groups build group savings through a micro-credit system and use accumulated savings to promote small-scale household activities.

List-II
(I) A product-sale venture from which participating women earn money.
(II) The agricultural content of the training.
(III) A use of accumulated group savings to support small-scale household activities.
(IV) The contribution sought through women’s active participation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Training in agricultural techniques and organic farming matches (II), while the project’s aim of women’s active participation in raising agricultural productivity and family income matches (IV). Making and selling vermicompost is the money-earning venture in (I). The accumulated savings used to promote small-scale household activities match (III).

A firm operates in the long run, input prices remain unchanged, and output increases successively through an initial range of increasing returns to scale (IRS), a middle range of constant returns to scale (CRS), and a final range of decreasing returns to scale (DRS). Consider the following statements about its long-run average cost (LRAC):
(A) During the IRS range, average cost falls as output increases.
(B) During the CRS range, average cost remains constant as output increases.
(C) During the DRS range, average cost falls as output increases.
(D) During the CRS range, average cost rises as output increases.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A), (B) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(A) and (D) only","(A) and (B) only"]
explanation: With input prices unchanged, average cost falls during IRS and remains constant during CRS. During DRS, average cost rises, so statement (C) is incorrect; statement (D) also contradicts the stated effect of CRS. Therefore, statements (A) and (B) are correct.

body: Environmental degradation can stem mainly from unstable use and inappropriate management practices. In a hypothetical audit, 360 cases are assigned to exactly one primary cause: 150 to unstable use, 100 to inappropriate management practices, and the rest to other causes. Among the cases assigned to either of the two named causes, what percentage is assigned to unstable use?
explanation: The two named causes account for 150 + 100 = 250 cases. Unstable use accounts for (150 ÷ 250) × 100 = 60% of those cases.

body:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Growth of aggregate real output during the first half of the twentieth century
(B) Growth of per capita output per year
(C) The colonial government’s attempt to estimate national and per capita income
(D) The estimator whose estimates during the colonial period were considered very significant
List-II
(I) V.K.R.V. Rao
(II) Less than 2 per cent
(III) No sincere attempt
(IV) Half per cent per year
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Aggregate real output growth is matched with less than 2 per cent, while per capita output growth per year is matched with half per cent. The colonial government made no sincere attempt to estimate national and per capita income, and V.K.R.V. Rao’s estimates were considered very significant. These matches give option D.

A workers’ collective earns a living through economic activities and includes an initiative addressing child labour in its work. Consider the following statements about the significance of the collective’s work:
(A) Its economic activities contribute to national income and development.
(B) Engaging in economic activities is part of earning a living.
(C) Work is undertaken only to earn a living.
(D) Work can also help address social issues such as child labour.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A), (B) and (C) only","(A), (C) and (D) only","(B), (C) and (D) only","(A), (B) and (D) only"]
explanation: Economic activities contribute to national income and development, and engaging in such activities is part of earning a living. Work is not only for earning a living; it can also help address social issues such as child labour. Therefore, statements (A), (B) and (D) are supported, while (C) is not.
